title: Physics Diagnostic — Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 (with Lower Secondary foundations)

levels.foundation: Lower-secondary basics (should be solid before grade 10)

questions.text: Name the SI units for length, mass and time.
What is the difference between a scalar and a vector quantity? Give an example of each.
How would you find the resultant of two forces acting at right angles to each other?
Calculate speed from distance and time (speed = distance / time).
On a distance–time graph, what does a steep line mean, and what does a flat (horizontal) line mean?
Define acceleration and calculate it from a change in velocity over time.
What does a speed–time graph show, and what does the area under it represent?
What is the approximate acceleration of free fall, g, near the Earth's surface?
What is the difference between mass and weight?
Calculate the weight of an object from its mass using W = mg.
Use the idea of density to explain why some objects float and others sink in water.
Calculate density from mass and volume; how would you measure the volume of an irregular stone?
Describe the effect of balanced and of unbalanced forces on the motion of an object.
How does the resultant force on an object relate to its mass and acceleration (F = ma)?
What are friction and air resistance, and how do they affect a moving object?
Identify a turning effect and calculate a moment (moment = force x distance).
State the conditions needed for an object to be in equilibrium.
Define momentum (p = mv) and calculate the momentum of a moving object.
State the principle of conservation of momentum and where it applies (e.g. a collision).
What is impulse, and how does it relate force, time and change in momentum?
Name several energy stores (kinetic, gravitational, chemical, thermal...) and describe one energy transfer.
State the principle of conservation of energy.
Calculate the work done by a force (W = force x distance) and state its unit.
Calculate kinetic energy, and the change in gravitational potential energy (mgh).
Define power (power = work done / time) and state its unit.
What is efficiency, and how is it calculated?
Define pressure and use pressure = force / area; why does a sharp knife cut more easily than a blunt one?
How does the pressure in a liquid change with depth and density (change in p = density x g x change in height)?
Use the particle model to explain how a gas exerts pressure.
Describe the arrangement and movement of particles in solids, liquids and gases.
Name the changes of state: melting, boiling, evaporation, condensation, freezing.
What is diffusion? Give an everyday example.
Use the kinetic model to explain how the pressure of a gas changes when it is heated or compressed.
What is the difference between heat (thermal energy) and temperature?
Describe thermal expansion of solids, liquids and gases, and give a everyday example.
Explain how evaporation causes cooling.
What is meant by specific heat capacity?
Describe conduction, convection and radiation, with an example of each.
Which way does thermal energy flow between hot and cold, and when does the net flow stop?
How can a house be designed or insulated to reduce heat loss by each method?
Define the amplitude, wavelength, frequency and period of a wave.
What is the difference between transverse and longitudinal waves? Give an example of each.
Use the wave equation, wave speed = frequency x wavelength.
Describe what happens when waves are reflected or refracted (e.g. in a ripple tank).
State the law of reflection and describe what happens to light at a plane mirror.
Describe refraction at an air-to-glass boundary in terms of change of speed; what is refractive index?
What is total internal reflection and the critical angle? Give a use (e.g. optical fibres).
Describe how a thin converging lens forms an image, and sketch a ray diagram.
What does a prism do to white light, and what does this tell us about white light?
List the regions of the electromagnetic spectrum in order of wavelength.
What speed do all electromagnetic waves travel at in a vacuum?
Give one use and one danger for two different regions (e.g. microwaves, gamma rays).
How does sound travel through air, and why can it not travel through a vacuum?
Explain an echo as the reflection of a sound wave.
On a waveform, which feature shows loudness and which shows pitch?
What is the approximate speed of sound in air, and how could you measure it?
What is a magnetic field, and where is it around a bar magnet?
What is the difference between a permanent magnet and induced magnetism, and between hard and soft magnetic materials?
How do you make an electromagnet, and how can you make it stronger?
What is electric charge, and what is the difference between a conductor and an insulator?
Define electric current, state its unit, and say how it is measured.
Define potential difference (voltage), state its unit, and say how a voltmeter is connected.
Define resistance and use the equation R = V / I; if 6 V drives 2 A, what is the resistance?
Recall and use the equation for electrical power, P = I x V.
Draw the standard symbols and a simple circuit with a cell, switch, lamp, ammeter and voltmeter.
How does the current behave in a series circuit compared with a parallel circuit?
Calculate the combined resistance of two resistors in series (and describe parallel).
What does a thermistor or a light-dependent resistor (LDR) do, and give a use.
State some electrical hazards in the home and explain the purpose of a fuse and of earthing.
What is electromagnetic induction, and how can you induce a voltage in a wire?
Describe how a simple electric motor works (the force on a current-carrying conductor in a field).
Describe how a transformer works and use the relationship between turns and voltage.

subtopics.name: 5.1 The nuclear model of the atom

questions.text: Describe the nuclear model of the atom: a small nucleus of protons and neutrons, with electrons around it.
What do proton (atomic) number and nucleon (mass) number mean? What is an isotope?
Read nuclide notation for an isotope and state its numbers of protons and neutrons.
What is background radiation? Name two sources of it.
Describe alpha, beta and gamma radiation and compare their penetrating powers.
What is meant by half-life? Use it in a simple calculation.
Give a use and a danger of radioactivity, and how sources should be handled safely.

subtopics.name: 6.1 The Earth and the Solar System

questions.text: Describe the Solar System: the Sun, the planets, moons, asteroids and comets.
Explain day and night, and the seasons, in terms of the Earth's rotation and orbit.
What keeps a planet in orbit, and how do orbital speed and time change with distance from the Sun?
What is a galaxy, and roughly how large is the Milky Way (in light-years)?
Describe the life cycle of a star like the Sun.
What is redshift, and how does it support the idea of an expanding Universe and the Big Bang?
